newsitem.title: USA: Little movement in U.S. interest rate swap spreads.
newsitem.headline: Little movement in U.S. interest rate swap spreads.

text.p: Spreads on U.S. interest rate swaps contnued to march in place for another week, dealers said.
Though spreads moved a few basis points around last month's Federal Reserve Board Open Market Committee meeting, nothing has moved in the week since.

On two-year LIBOR swaps, spreads were quoted at 17 basis points bid, 20 basis points offered, unchanged from a week ago. Three-year swaps were also unchanged, with spreads quoted at 19 basis points bid, 21 to 22 basis points offered.
At the middle of the swap curve, spreads on five-year swaps were quoted at 25 to 26 basis points bid, 27 to 28 basis points offered, about one basis point wider than a week ago.
At 10 years, spreads were quoted at 34 basis points bid, 36 basis points offered, also about one basis point wider on the week.

U.S. Treasury will auction $10 billion of new 10-year notes on Tuesday. But little impact was seen on swaps as the new notes were yielding within one-tenth of one basis point of the on-the-run 10-year note.
With no repo special expected to develop around the auction, traders said the auction's impact on swap spreads should remain muted.
On very long-term deals, one dealer said 30-year spreads were in a range of 38 to 40 basis points.
